messages:
maria-support: Hey team — customer acme-telemetry on dedicated-us-west started seeing 429s ~09:14 UTC after their subscription conversion. They say the Console shows "quota: 3,600 min" but the API errors show quota_exceeded with limit=60. Can someone triage? sample req id: r_3f7b

kevin-sre: Looking. Need last 20 log lines and confirm whether they changed billing plan or just had an account model migration.

maria-support: They did a guided migration from legacy-minute to usage-based yesterday (self-serve). Pasted last logs:
```
2026-02-20T09:13:58Z quota_check: tenant=acme-telemetry limit=60 denom=TOKENS used=60 result=DENIED req=r_3f7b
2026-02-20T09:13:59Z request: id=r_3f7b model=gpt-small latency=31ms status=429
2026-02-20T09:14:05Z quota_check: tenant=acme-telemetry limit=60 denom=TOKENS used=61 result=DENIED req=r_3f80
```
Console screenshot (they uploaded) literally shows "3,600 minutes remaining".

olivia-eng-runtime: That pattern screams unit/denom translation failure in the migration converter. If a minutes-based quota integer is naively copied into a TOKEN denom field without scaling, you end up with a 60x under-provisioning. Tagging @kevin-sre for infra checks.

autoscale-bot: [alert] pool=dedicated-us-west queue_depth=9 throttle_rate=0.72 scale_action=NO_SCALE reason="queue under scaling threshold (threshold=15) despite throttling"

james-support: Short-term mitigation options: 1) tenant admin override to raise quota, 2) route tenant to overflow pool, or 3) temporary bypass of quota checks for specific routes. I'd prefer override first.

kevin-sre: I'll apply a modest tenant override (x20) and watch for noisy-neighbor. Applying conservative override now.

kevin-sre: override applied -> tenant=acme-telemetry quota_units=120000 denom=TOKENS override_by=kevin-sre reason="temp-after-migration-fix"

maria-support: Customer reports 429 rate dropped substantially after the override, but they're still seeing occasional spikes when batch jobs kick off. They're concerned about latency and user-facing errors.

olivia-eng-runtime: Investigation update: migration script expected field name "time_limit_minutes" but older tenant records used "window_minutes". The migration transform had a guard that if it couldn't find the time field it would default denom to TOKENS and copy the numeric literal without conversion. So 3600 (minutes) became 3600 tokens instead of 3600 * avg_tokens_per_minute (~60) => ~216,000 tokens. Off by ~60x.

kevin-sre: Plan of action: 1) patch migration to check both "time_limit_minutes" and "window_minutes" and perform minutes->tokens scaling using our historical avg_tokens_per_minute metric (we'll use 60 as default), 2) run a safe backfill for tenants whose denom mismatches are detected, 3) add unit/integration tests and a canary job before rolling the migration script. Also add an alert to flag denom mismatch between Console and runtime.

james-support: Can we also add a read-only column in Console that shows "effective_tokens" so customers and CS can validate? Would help reduce confusion.

kevin-sre: Good idea. I'll add it to the backlog for the Console team. For immediate follow-up: INC-2026-459 created, PR #5591 submitted for migration patch, and a hotfix job prepared to backfill affected tenants tonight in maintenance window. Dashboards updated to show denom mapping errors and recent backfill runs.

maria-support: I'll notify acme-telemetry that we applied a temporary override and outline timeline: hotfix/backfill tonight, permanent fix + tests tomorrow, postmortem within 48h. They want a customer-facing summary.

olivia-eng-runtime: Adding note: we measured avg_tokens_per_minute across similar workloads = 60 +/- 10; we'll use 60 as conservative multiplier for conversion. Also logging will include original migration payload for audit.

kevin-sre: Monitoring note: keeping override conservative. If noisy neighbor signs appear (latency increase or eviction events), we'll throttle back the override and switch customer to overflow routing.

maria-support: Thanks — I'll send the customer update and request they validate normal traffic tomorrow after backfill. :thumbsup:
